title: Effect of music-based training on cognitive function in older adults with and without neurological impairment: a systematic review
abstract: Aging is associated with progressive decline in cognitive skills. Combining music-based interventions has been proposed as a strategy to enhance cognitive processing in older adults. The objective of the study was to review the effects of music-based training on cognitive outcomes in healthy and neurologically impaired older adults. A comprehensive literature search was conducted. Randomized controlled trials investigating music-based training (dual, multi-task) and reporting cognitive outcomes were included. Methodological quality and risk of bias was evaluated. Data were synthesized qualitatively. Seven randomized controlled trials were included. Interventions included music-based dual-task, and multitask musicmovement programs with durations from single-session to 12-month protocols. Methodological quality ranged from fair to good, while Cochrane RoB2 assessments indicated some concerns in allocation and outcome reporting. Most studies reported improvements in specific cognitive domains. Music based intervention shows promise for improving cognitive domains in older adults. Larger, high-quality studies with standardized protocols and longer follow-up required.
